extraction.method: Manual-assisted static inspection of every preprocessor macro in ini.h/ini.c, cross-checked against README.md, meson_options.txt, meson.build and tests/meson.build. Inertness ('active_when') verified by comparing gcc -E output of ini.c with and without the option. Lower bounds of integer ranges verified empirically with -fsanitize=address,undefined (value below the bound crashes or triggers UB).

options.description: Nonzero: the ini_handler callback receives the line number as a fifth parameter. Changes the public callback type, so client code (including test drivers) must be written for the matching signature.

source_location.note: Default and the two ini_handler typedefs.

options.description: Nonzero: indented non-blank lines are continuations of the previous name's value (Python configparser style); the handler is called again with the same name.
Nonzero: skip a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) at the start of line 1.
Set of characters that start a whole-line comment (tested with strchr on the first non-blank character).

discrete_settings.label: default
discrete_settings.rationale: Both configparser comment characters.

discrete_settings.label: semicolon-only
discrete_settings.rationale: Lines starting with '#' become name/value lines -- interacts with ALLOW_NO_VALUE and inline comments.

discrete_settings.label: hash-only
discrete_settings.rationale: Lines starting with ';' are no longer comments; ';' is the default inline prefix, so this probes the start-vs-inline prefix interaction.

discrete_settings.label: none
discrete_settings.rationale: Empty set: no start-of-line comments at all (strchr("", '\0') still matches blank lines, so blank lines are unaffected).

options.discretization_rationale: Open string domain (any character set). Partitioned by which of the two conventional comment characters are recognised: both / only ';' / only '#' / neither. Exotic prefixes (e.g. '[' or '=') are excluded because they redefine core syntax rather than comment handling.

options.description: Nonzero: a character from INI_INLINE_COMMENT_PREFIXES that follows whitespace ends the value/section text. Zero matches Python 3.2+ configparser.
Characters that start an inline comment (only when inline comments are enabled).

discrete_settings.label: hash-only
discrete_settings.rationale: Disjoint from the default; probes values containing ';'.

discrete_settings.label: both
discrete_settings.rationale: Union; values containing ' #' get truncated.

options.discretization_rationale: Open string domain. Partitioned like INI_START_COMMENT_PREFIXES by which conventional comment characters are included; the empty set is omitted because it is behaviourally equivalent to INI_ALLOW_INLINE_COMMENTS=0 (the strchr test can never succeed).

options.description: Nonzero: fixed INI_MAX_LINE-byte line buffer on the stack. Zero: heap buffer from (ini_)malloc, sized INI_INITIAL_ALLOC, optionally growing (INI_ALLOW_REALLOC).
Maximum line buffer size in bytes (must be 3 more than the longest line: '\r', '\n', NUL). Overlong lines are discarded through a 16-byte 'abyss' buffer and reported as an error.

valid_range.evidence: INI_MAX_LINE=1 makes the 'line too long' test read line[-1] (UBSan: index out of bounds, ini.c:166). Upper bound is INT_MAX because the size is passed to the reader as (int)max_line.

discrete_settings.label: min-boundary
discrete_settings.rationale: Smallest legal buffer: one character per read, every non-empty line overflows.

discrete_settings.label: small
discrete_settings.rationale: Value used by developer variants (multi_max_line, string, heap_max_line); several test lines exceed it, exercising the overflow/discard path.

discrete_settings.label: large
discrete_settings.rationale: Larger than every test input line; the overflow path is unreachable.

options.discretization_rationale: Equivalence partitions relative to input line length L: buffer degenerate (2), buffer < L+3 for some inputs (20), typical default (200), buffer >> L for all inputs (4096). 2 is the lower boundary; 1 is an invalid boundary value (UB) and is excluded.

options.description: Size in bytes (including NUL) of the section-name buffer. Longer names are silently truncated.

valid_range.evidence: INI_MAX_SECTION=0 declares char section[0]; ini_strncpy0 computes size-1 = SIZE_MAX and overflows the stack buffer (ASan stack-buffer-overflow).

discrete_settings.label: min-boundary
discrete_settings.rationale: Every section name is truncated to the empty string.

discrete_settings.label: small
discrete_settings.rationale: Shorter than most section names in the test inputs; truncation path exercised on common inputs.

discrete_settings.label: default
discrete_settings.rationale: tests/long_section.ini (62 chars) is truncated.

discrete_settings.label: large
discrete_settings.rationale: No test input is truncated.

options.discretization_rationale: Partitions relative to section-name length N: always-truncate (1), truncate typical names (8), truncate only long names (50, default), never truncate (256). Note the developer driver itself truncates section names to 49 chars (char Prev_section[50]), which masks differences above 50 in its golden output.

options.description: Size in bytes (including NUL) of the stored previous-name buffer. It is only used to remember the name for multi-line continuations; names passed to the handler for name=value lines are never truncated.

valid_range.evidence: INI_MAX_NAME=0 triggers an out-of-bounds access in ini_strncpy0 (UBSan).

discrete_settings.label: min-boundary
discrete_settings.rationale: prev_name is always empty, which silently disables multi-line continuation.

discrete_settings.label: small
discrete_settings.rationale: Continuation lines are reported under a truncated name that differs from the original key.

options.discretization_rationale: Same partitioning as INI_MAX_SECTION, relative to property-name length. The minimum boundary is behaviourally significant: with INI_MAX_NAME=1 the '*prev_name' guard is always false.

options.description: Nonzero: the heap line buffer doubles (via ini_realloc) up to INI_MAX_LINE when a line does not fit. Only applies when INI_USE_STACK=0.
Initial heap line-buffer size. Without realloc it is the effective maximum line size (INI_MAX_LINE is then ignored).

valid_range.evidence: INI_INITIAL_ALLOC=1 reads line[-1] in the overflow check (ASan heap-buffer-overflow), with and without INI_ALLOW_REALLOC.

discrete_settings.label: min-boundary
discrete_settings.rationale: With realloc the buffer must double repeatedly; without realloc every line overflows.

discrete_settings.label: tiny
discrete_settings.rationale: Developer value for heap_realloc variants.

discrete_settings.label: small
discrete_settings.rationale: Developer value for heap_max_line / heap_string variants.

discrete_settings.label: default
discrete_settings.rationale: Equal to the default INI_MAX_LINE.

options.discretization_rationale: Partitions relative to line length and to INI_MAX_LINE: degenerate (2), far below typical lines so realloc always triggers (5), around INI_MAX_LINE=20 (20), default (200). The developer suite also uses 12 (alloc variant); it is legal (inside valid_range) but treated as off-partition.

options.description: Nonzero: stop reading after the first line that sets the error code (parse error, overlong line or handler returning 0).
Nonzero: call the handler with name=NULL, value=NULL at every [section] line.
Nonzero: a line with a name but no '=' or ':' calls the handler with value=NULL instead of being a parse error.
Nonzero: use client-supplied ini_malloc/ini_free(/ini_realloc) instead of the C library. The client must define and link these symbols.
Which public parse function the client calls. All five funnel into ini_parse_stream() but differ in the reader (fgets vs in-memory string reader) and in error reporting (-1 file open, -3 ferror).

discrete_settings.label: default
discrete_settings.rationale: Filename API; used by tests/unittest.c and the README examples.
FILE* API; adds the ferror() -> -3 path.
Custom ini_reader callback (an fgets wrapper in the driver).
NUL-terminated buffer through ini_reader_string().
Explicit-length buffer through ini_reader_string().

options.description: What the client's ini_handler returns. A zero return marks the line as an error (and stops parsing when INI_STOP_ON_FIRST_ERROR=1). The library has no default; the model default is the convention of the developer driver tests/unittest.c.

discrete_settings.label: default
discrete_settings.rationale: Developer convention: fail only on user=parse_error (tests/user_error.ini).
Typical lenient client (tests/unittest_string.c, examples).
Every callback fails, including section callbacks; maximises interaction with STOP_ON_FIRST_ERROR and CALL_HANDLER_ON_NEW_SECTION.

source_location.note: Handler should return nonzero on success, zero on error.
Return value consumed at each HANDLER() call site.

constraints.rationale: Documented contract: a custom allocator requires the heap line buffer. In code the macro is merely ignored on the stack path (gcc -E output identical), but the documentation states it as a requirement, so the model treats the combination as invalid.

constraints.expression: if INI_USE_STACK == 0 and INI_ALLOW_REALLOC == 1 then INI_INITIAL_ALLOC <= INI_MAX_LINE
constraints.rationale: The buffer is documented to grow *to* INI_MAX_LINE. If the initial size already exceeds it, the growth loop never runs and lines longer than INI_MAX_LINE are accepted, so INI_MAX_LINE no longer bounds line length. Builds and runs without error.

constraints.expression: if INI_USE_STACK == 0 and INI_ALLOW_REALLOC == 0 then INI_INITIAL_ALLOC == INI_MAX_LINE
constraints.rationale: On the heap without realloc the line limit is INI_INITIAL_ALLOC and INI_MAX_LINE is ignored entirely (verified: gcc -E output identical for different INI_MAX_LINE). Setting them differently means the configured maximum line length is not the enforced one. The developer variant heap_max_line sets both to 20 for exactly this reason. Documentation is itself inconsistent here: the ini.h comment for INI_ALLOW_REALLOC says the non-realloc buffer is INI_MAX_LINE bytes, while README.md and the code use INI_INITIAL_ALLOC.

evidence.note: Claims a fixed-size buffer of INI_MAX_LINE bytes when realloc is off.
Says the fixed buffer is INI_INITIAL_ALLOC bytes.

excluded_options.reason: Symbol-visibility attribute (__attribute__((visibility("default"))) or __declspec). No behavioural effect on parsing; overriding it only changes linkage.
Windows/Cygwin DLL import/export only; not applicable on the Linux build host.

Packaging and build-orchestration options, not variability of the parser. Notable interaction for the study: with distro_install=true (the meson default) meson.build ignores every feature option above, so meson users get defaults regardless of what they set.
Separate component (cpp/INIReader.cpp) built on top of ini_parse; GetBoolean/GetInteger parse values but are not configuration options of the parser. Out of SUT scope (ini.c).

test_suite.oracle: Golden-output diff: each developer variant is a driver compiled with specific -D flags whose stdout must equal a checked-in baseline file (tests/runtest.sh, tests/unittest.sh).

drivers.notes: Parses the 13 input files with ini_parse(). Supports both handler signatures.
Handler has the 4-argument signature only; with INI_HANDLER_LINENO=1 it is an incompatible-pointer-type warning under GCC 13 and an error from GCC 14, and calling it is undefined behaviour.
Exercises the ferror() -> -3 path by reading a write-only stream.

Runtime-configurable re-host of unittest.c plus 9 generated inputs. Oracles: developer baseline (when handler policy matches) and a differential oracle comparing the selected entry point against a reference entry point on every input.
